---
title: "Demo: Loading Macros via include shortcode"
format:
  html: default
  revealjs:
    output-file: demo-shortcode-slides.html
---

This page demonstrates the [`include` shortcode](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/includes.html) strategy for loading macros into a Quarto document.

The include shortcode embeds the contents of another file inline at the point of insertion. To load LaTeX macro definitions, the shortcode is wrapped in a `$$...$$` math block inside a hidden div:

````qmd
::: {.hidden}
$$
{{< include macros/macros.qmd >}}
$$
:::
````

The `::: {.hidden}` div ([Quarto's recommended pattern](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html#equations) for custom TeX macros) hides the block from the rendered page. The `$$...$$` delimiters cause Quarto's MathJax renderer to process the included content as LaTeX, registering all `\def`-based macro definitions globally for use throughout the document.

> **Note:** This demo places the include shortcode directly in the document (since `macros.qmd` is in the same directory). When using this repository as a submodule, the path would be `macros/macros.qmd`.

> **Note (MathJax limitations):** [Quarto's MathJax integration](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html#equations) supports `\def`, `\newcommand`, `\renewcommand`, `\newenvironment`, `\renewenvironment`, and `\let` — but **not** `\providecommand`. Since `macros.qmd` uses `\providecommand` for many definitions, those macros are silently ignored for HTML/RevealJS output. The example table below uses only `\def`-based macros, which render correctly.

> **Note (PDF/docx):** This demo does not include PDF or docx output. The `$$...$$` wrapping causes LaTeX to interpret the included content as a display math equation rather than preamble definitions, so the shortcode approach does not work for PDF macro loading. Word documents do not support LaTeX/MathJax macros at all. Use the [`include-in-header` strategy](demo-include-in-header.qmd) for PDF output.

> **Note (RevealJS blank slide):** The hidden include block below appears before the first section heading. In RevealJS output, content before the first `##` heading becomes a blank title slide. This is a [known limitation](https://github.com/orgs/quarto-dev/discussions/8376) of the shortcode approach for RevealJS. For RevealJS without a blank slide, use the [`include-in-header` strategy](demo-include-in-header.qmd) instead.

::: {.hidden}
$$
{{< include macros.qmd >}}
$$
:::

## Example math

The table below uses macros defined with `\def` in `macros.qmd`, which work in HTML and RevealJS output:

| Description | Code | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Greek: alpha | `$\a$` | $\a$ |
| Greek: beta | `$\b$` | $\b$ |
| Greek: gamma | `$\g$` | $\g$ |
| Greek: lambda | `$\l$` | $\l$ |
| Greek: sigma | `$\s$` | $\s$ |
| Log-likelihood | `$\llik$` | $\llik$ |
| Independent | `$X \ind Y$` | $X \ind Y$ |
| IID distributed | `$X_i \siid \Normal(\m, \ss)$` | $X_i \siid \Normal(\m, \ss)$ |
| Vector: mu | `$\vm$` | $\vm$ |
| Hat beta | `$\hb$` | $\hb$ |
